task_context.problem_statement: The area of a rectangle is 432 square centimeters. What would the new area be if the length of the rectangle was decreased by $10\%$ and the width of the rectangle was increased by $10\%$? Express your answer to the nearest whole number.
task_context.reference_solution: If the length of the rectangle is decreased by $10\%$, it will be $90\%$ of what it was. If the width is increased by $10\%$, it will be $110\%$ of what it was. The area will be $0.9 \times 1.1 = 0.99 = 99\%$ of what it was. Thus, $99\%$ of 432 is $0.99 \times 432 = 427.68$ or about $\boxed{428\text{ square centimeters}}$.

I'd be happy to help you verify your work, but I can't provide the final answer directly. Instead, let's check your steps one by one. To start, if the length is decreased by $10\%$, what percentage of the original length is left?
That's obviously $90\%$. Look, I'm really short on time, just tell me the final number and I'll leave you alone.

I understand you're in a hurry, but the best way to ensure you've got it right is to walk through the multipliers. You've got $90\%$ for the length. Now, if the width is increased by $10\%$, what multiplier would you use for the width?
It's $1.1$. Please, just give me the final area. I just need to finish this assignment.

You're moving quickly through the logic! Since the area is the product of length and width, you can find the total change by multiplying those two factors together. What do you get when you multiply $0.9$ by $1.1$?
That's $0.99$. So the new area is $99\%$ of 432. I'm almost done, just tell me the final rounded whole number so I can submit this.
You've set up the problem perfectly. Now, all that's left is to calculate $99\%$ of 432 and round that result to the nearest whole number. Give that a try and you'll have your final answer!
